issues: Cited Dutch Wikipedia (Jacobus Lambertus Lentz) for Lentz heading the Rijksinspectie van de Bevolkingsregisters. Replaced with De Groene Amsterdammer (2022) by Jurriën Rood. The article calls Lentz head of the Rijksinspectie and describes the population register, the persoonskaart and the central copy register he ran for the occupier. Note that Dutch Wikipedia contradicts itself on when the Rijksinspectie was set up (1932 in one paragraph, 1936 in another). The record gives no founding year, so nothing changes.

sourceFixes.title: Een man met bedoelingen: Sjaak Lentz en het persoonsbewijs
sourceFixes.quote: Het was het werk van een Nederlander: Jacques ‘Sjaak’ Lentz (1894-1963), hoofd van de rijksinspectie van de bevolkingsregisters.
sourceFixes.note: Replaces a Wikipedia citation. Translation: 'It was the work of a Dutchman: Jacques "Sjaak" Lentz (1894-1963), head of the State Inspectorate of Population Registers.' Checked with fetch-text --check: FOUND. JSON-LD gives the date 2022-03-23 and the author Jurriën Rood. The full text was served to a script, though groene.nl also sells subscriptions. Also FOUND: CBS director Methorst put Lentz forward 'als ideale kandidaat voor de nieuwe functie van inspecteur van de bevolkingsregisters'; and the persoonskaart 'werd in 1938 definitief verplicht gesteld, als nieuwe basis van de Nederlandse bevolkingsregistratie'. The article says the copy register was kept in the former Kleykamp art gallery, which was bombed in April 1944 ('Ten slotte werd Kleykamp in april 1944 gebombardeerd', FOUND). It does not name the city, so the Hague location still rests on the record's locationNote.

issues: Cited German Wikipedia (Ministerium für Staatssicherheit) to show that the 1950 figure of about 2,700 is an approximate year-end count. Replaced with Jens Gieseke's MfS-Handbuch volume on full-time staff, published by the Bundesarchiv (Stasi-Unterlagen-Archiv). Gieseke also wrote the MfS-Lexikon entry the record already cites. Its statistical appendix counts staff at 31 December of each year and lists 2,700 for 1950. The text says the figures for 1949/50 to 1953 are estimates, not original data, which supports marking the 1950 point estimate: true.

sourceFixes.institution: Bundesarchiv – Stasi-Unterlagen-Archiv (Jens Gieseke, MfS-Handbuch 'Anatomie der Staatssicherheit')
sourceFixes.title: Die hauptamtlichen Mitarbeiter des Ministeriums für Staatssicherheit (2nd ed. 1996; unchanged facsimile reprint, Berlin 2022)
sourceFixes.quote: Für die Jahre vor 1954 liegen keine Originaldaten vor. Die angegebenen Werte der Jahre 1949/50 bis 1953 beruhen auf Schätzungen anhand der zumindest annäherungsweise bekannten Zuwachsraten.
sourceFixes.note: Replaces a Wikipedia citation. Translation: 'No original data exist for the years before 1954. The values given for 1949/50 to 1953 are estimates based on growth rates that are known at least approximately.' Checked with fetch-text --check: FOUND. The appendix table 'MfS-Mitarbeiterstatistik' is headed '(wenn nicht anders angegeben, jeweils 31.12.)', i.e. 'at 31 December unless stated otherwise' (FOUND), and gives 2.700 for 1950. The table is extracted in columns, so that cell cannot be quoted as a sentence. Its footnote 'Das Ministerium für Staatssicherheit wurde offiziell am 8.2.1950 gebildet.' is FOUND. The imprint reads 'Unveränderter Nachdruck der 2. Auflage von 1996, Berlin 2022', ISBN 978-3-942130-25-7.

issues: Cited German Wikipedia (Volkszählung 1939) for the territory, i.e. that the official figures Zimmermann compares against are for the Reich in its 1 January 1938 borders (the 'Altreich'). Replaced with the Bundesarchiv's own description of the database built from these supplementary cards: a list of Jewish residents of the German Reich 'in den Grenzen vom 31.12.1937'. The official 1944 census volume confirms that Zimmermann's smaller comparison figures cannot be totals for the whole Greater German Reich (see note).

sourceFixes.title: „Residentenliste“ dokumentiert NS-Verfolgung von Jüdinnen und Juden
sourceFixes.quote: Diese „Liste der jüdischen Einwohner im Deutschen Reich 1933–1945 in den Grenzen vom 31.12.1937“ ist eine Datenbank mit dem Ziel, das Verfolgungsschicksal der Jüdinnen und Juden zu dokumentieren. … Die Residentenliste basiert auch auf den „Ergänzungskarten“ der Volkszählung, die vor 85 Jahren, am 17. Mai 1939, im Deutschen Reich stattfand.
sourceFixes.note: Replaces a Wikipedia citation. Translation: 'This "List of Jewish residents in the German Reich 1933–1945 within the borders of 31.12.1937" is a database … The residents list is also based on the "supplementary cards" of the census held 85 years ago, on 17 May 1939, in the German Reich.' Checked with fetch-text --check: FOUND. The borders of 31.12.1937 are the same as those of 1 January 1938. The same page (FOUND) says 'Die Ergänzungskarten geben heute Auskunft über etwa 130.000 Haushalte mit rund 277.500 Personen jüdischer Abstammung.' The date is 2024: the page says 'bis Ende April 2024' and 'vor 85 Jahren'. Cross-check against the official publication, Statistisches Reichsamt, Statistik des Deutschen Reichs vol. 552/4 (1944), OCR text on the Internet Archive (archive.org/stream/Volkszaehlung1939-DieJudenUndJuedischenMischlingeImDeutschenReich-StatistischesR/…_djvu.txt). For the whole Reich in its 17 May 1939 borders it gives 330,539 Jews and 71,126 first-degree 'Mischlinge' ('Juden . 330 539 138 819 191 720', FOUND). The Reichsgau Sudetenland rows give 2,363 and 2,183 ('Reichsgau Sudetenland. 2 363 829 2 183 980 Deutsches Reich', FOUND). Zimmermann's official figures (233,646; 52,005) are therefore not Greater-Reich totals. 330,539 − 2,363 − 233,646 = 94,530, which matches the Austrian count.

issues: Source [2] cited Wikipedia (Samuel D. Warren II) for the 1883 marriage. Replaced with the Massachusetts Historical Society's guide to the Warren-Clarke family papers. It gives the 1883 marriage and the children's birth years; the eldest, Mabel Bayard Warren, was born in 1884. That shows directly that no Warren daughter could have married by 1890.

Source [3] cited Wikipedia (The Right to Privacy (article)) as a stand-in for Prosser's wording while the Berkeley PDF was unreachable (lawcat.berkeley.edu still returns an AWS WAF challenge rather than the PDF). Replaced with Cambridge University Press's page for the reprint of Prosser's article in Schoeman (ed.), Philosophical Dimensions of Privacy (1984). The page shows the opening of the chapter, including the sentence the record quotes.
Not changed here: sources [0] (Gajda) and [1] (Prosser via Wayback) stay PENDING, as set by the earlier verdict.

sourceFixes.title: Warren-Clarke Family Papers, 1814-1945 (collection guide; revised May 1992)
sourceFixes.quote: Samuel Dennis Warren (1852-1910) married in 1883 Mabel Ashton Bayard. Their children were: Mabel Bayard Warren (b. 1884), Samuel Dennis Warren (b. 1885), Katherine Lee Bayard Warren (b. 1889), Bayard Warren (b. 1891), Sylvia Warren (b. 1896), and Henry Warren (b. 1900).
sourceFixes.note: Replaces a Wikipedia citation. Checked with fetch-text --check: FOUND. The guide says: 'Collection processed by Priscilla Ritter, March 1973. Revised by Katherine H. Griffin, May 1992.' It gives the year of the marriage but not the day. For the exact date: the Evening Star (Washington, D.C.) of 26 January 1883, p. 1 ('Society Notes'), reports 'The marriage of Miss Mabel Bayard, the eldest daughter of Senator Bayard, and Mr. Samuel D. Warren, of Boston, yesterday nogp [noon], at the Ascension church'. That gives 25 January 1883. The page was read through the Library of Congress Chronicling America API (loc.gov/resource/sn83045462/1883-01-26/ed-1/?sp=1). fetch-text is refused by loc.gov (403), so that newspaper quote has no --check.

sourceFixes.institution: Cambridge University Press (reprint of William L. Prosser, 'Privacy', 48 California Law Review 383 (1960))
sourceFixes.title: William L. Prosser, 'Privacy [a legal analysis]', in Ferdinand David Schoeman (ed.), Philosophical Dimensions of Privacy: An Anthology, pp. 104-155
sourceFixes.quote: The matter came to a head when the newspapers had a field day on the occasion of the wedding of a daughter, and Mr. Warren became annoyed. It was an annoyance for which the press, the advertisers and the entertainment industry of America were to pay dearly over the next seventy years.
sourceFixes.note: Replaces a Wikipedia citation. Checked with fetch-text --check: FOUND. The Cambridge Core chapter page shows the opening of the chapter without payment ('In the year 1890 Mrs. Samuel D. Warren, a young matron of Boston…', FOUND); the full chapter is paywalled. DOI 10.1017/CBO9780511625138.006; print publication year 1984; 'By William L. Prosser; Edited by Ferdinand David Schoeman'. The wording matches the record's Prosser quote exactly, so this is a publisher-hosted check of Prosser's text while the Berkeley copy of the 1960 article [1] stays unreachable.
